operation.description:
What the task does:

- `document_processing`: an indexing task.
- `document_reindex`, `document_upload`, `document_delete`: a bulk task. Bulk uploads and deletions come from Dify; a deletion over this API creates a deletion job instead.
- `source_sync`, `source_crawl_preview`, `source_crawl_import`, `source_online_document_import`, `source_online_drive_import`: a source run.

progress_completed.description: Items completed: the document of an indexing task, the documents of a bulk task, or the items of a source run.

progress_percent.description: Progress from 0 to 100. For an indexing task it follows the task's stage.

progress_total.description: Items in the task, counted like `progress_completed`. `1` for an indexing task.

semantic_enrichment.description: Knowledge graph building status for an indexing task's content. Deep and Research searches follow the knowledge graph. `null` for other kinds.

source_title.description: Name of the source of a source run. Set only when listing without `task_ids`.

state.description:
`queued`, `running`, `completed`, `failed`, or `canceled`, mapped from the task's own state:

- An indexing task is `completed` once it has published, even while its semantic enrichment is still running.
- A crawl preview waiting for its pages to be selected is `completed`.

For the exact state, read an indexing task with [Get Indexing Task](/en/api-reference/indexing-tasks/get-indexing-task) and a source run with [Get Source Run](/en/api-reference/source-syncs-and-imports/get-source-run).

task_kind.description: `document` (an indexing task), `document_bulk` (a bulk task), or `source` (a source run).

updated_at.description: When the task last changed, ISO 8601.

kind.description: What the chunk was built from: `chunk` for a run of body text (the default), `section` for a heading section, `table` for a table, `image` for an image, `summary` for a generated summary.

knowledge_space_id.description: Internal ID of the knowledge base. Not the knowledge base ID in the path.

ordinal.description: Position of the chunk within the revision, starting at `0`. Sort by it to read chunks in document order.

parent_chunk_id.description: ID of the parent chunk for parent-child chunking. `null` for top-level chunks.

parse_element_ids.description: IDs of the parsed elements the chunk was built from.

section_path.description: Headings from the document root to the chunk's section.

start_offset.description: Zero-based UTF-8 byte offset in the parsed document text. Inclusive start. `null` when unknown.

status_url.description: URL of [Get Deletion Job](/en/api-reference/deletion-jobs/get-deletion-job) for this job: absolute when the deployment sets `SERVICE_API_URL`, otherwise a path that starts with `/v1/`. The same value is sent in the `Location` response header.

batch_id.description: ID of the batch that records this request.

status_url.description: URL of the file's job in [Get Deletion Job](/en/api-reference/deletion-jobs/get-deletion-job).

results.description: One entry per requested file, with its outcome.

error.description: Why the file was rejected. `null` otherwise.

job.description: The deletion job when `status` is `accepted`. `null` otherwise.

status.description:
- `accepted`: deletion was accepted, and `job` and `status_url` are set.
- `rejected`: the file was not deleted. `error` says why.
- `pending`: the file was not accepted yet. To retry it, send the original request again with the same `Idempotency-Key`.

status_url.description: URL of [Get Deletion Job](/en/api-reference/deletion-jobs/get-deletion-job) for the file's job. `null` unless `status` is `accepted`.

URL of [Get Deletion Batch](/en/api-reference/deletion-jobs/get-deletion-batch) for this batch: absolute when the deployment sets `SERVICE_API_URL`, otherwise a path that starts with `/v1/`. [Delete Document Files in Batch](/en/api-reference/documents-and-chunks/delete-document-files-in-batch) also sends it in the `Location` response header.

total.description: Number of files in the original request.

checkpoint.description: How far the deletion has progressed: `requested` (newly accepted), then `quiescing`, `deleting_objects`, `deleting_derived_data`, `deleting_primary_data`, and `completed`.

completed_at.description: When the job completed, ISO 8601. `null` until then, and on a `failed` job.

created_at.description: When the job was accepted, ISO 8601.

error.description: The last error, or `null` when there is none. It is also set while `run_state` is `retry_wait`, so read `run_state`, not `error`, to tell whether the job failed.

message.description: Public message for the last error. Internal error details are omitted.

retryable.description: `true` when `run_state` is `failed`. This API can't retry a failed deletion.

knowledge_space_id.description: Internal ID of the knowledge base. Not the knowledge base ID in the path.

mode.description: How a source deletion treats the source's documents: `cascade` deletes them, `keep` keeps them. On a document file deletion it says nothing about what the deletion removes.

progress.description: Item counts of a multi-item deletion. Not populated by this API. Always `null`.

current_item_kind.description: Kind of the item being deleted.

retry_at.description: When the next automatic retry runs, ISO 8601. `null` when none is scheduled.

run_state.description:
Scheduler state:

- `dispatch_pending` (newly accepted), `queued`, `running`: in progress.
- `retry_wait`: an automatic retry is scheduled at `retry_at`.
- `completed`: everything was removed.
- `failed`: cleanup stopped, and the target stays hidden. It can't be retried.

target_id.description: ID of the target: the document file ID for `document`, the source ID for `source`.

target_type.description: What the job deletes: `document` for a document file, `source` for a source.

updated_at.description: When the job last changed, ISO 8601.

active.description: The active revision: the content the knowledge base serves. active_revision.description: Number of the active revision. `null` while none is active.

created_at.description: When the document was created, ISO 8601.

disabled_at.description: When the document was disabled in Dify, ISO 8601.

disabled_by_subject_id.description: Internal ID of whoever disabled the document. Not needed to call this API.

enabled.description: `false` after the document is disabled in Dify. [Re-index Documents](/en/api-reference/documents-and-chunks/re-index-documents) skips disabled documents.

id.description: Document ID. It stays the same when the document's content is updated.

knowledge_space_id.description: Internal ID of the knowledge base. Not the knowledge base ID in the path.

latest_task.description: The newest indexing task behind the document's revisions, with `task_kind: document`. Follow it with [Get Document Indexing Task](/en/api-reference/indexing-tasks/get-document-indexing-task) using its `id`. `null` when there is none, and always `null` in the [Update Document Metadata](/en/api-reference/documents-and-chunks/update-document-metadata) response.

provider_item_id.description: For a document imported from a source, the item's identifier there: the `providerItemId` sent to [Import Source Items](/en/api-reference/source-syncs-and-imports/import-source-items), or the `page_id` of a website page.

row_version.description: Change counter. Send it as `expectedRowVersion` on [Update Document Metadata](/en/api-reference/documents-and-chunks/update-document-metadata). It increases on metadata updates, when a new revision becomes active, and when the document is enabled or disabled in Dify.

source_id.description: Source the document came from. `null` for uploaded files.

status.description: `pending` (no revision active yet), `ready` (a revision is active), `failed` (the first revision failed to index and none is active), or `deleting`. A `ready` document stays `ready` when a later revision fails.

updated_at.description: When the document last changed, ISO 8601.

user_metadata.description: Custom metadata, keyed by metadata field name. Change it with [Update Document Metadata](/en/api-reference/documents-and-chunks/update-document-metadata) or in Dify.

created_at.description: When the file was stored, ISO 8601.

id.description: Document file ID. Different from the document ID in the address bar of the open document in Dify.

knowledge_space_id.description: Internal ID of the knowledge base. Not the knowledge base ID in the path.

metadata.description: Metadata recorded with the file when it was uploaded or imported.

object_key.description: Key of the file in object storage. No operation in this API returns the file's content.

parser_status.description: Parse state of this version of the file: `pending`, `parsed`, or `failed`. Parsing is one step of indexing. A `parsed` file can still have no outline and no chunks.

sha256.description: SHA-256 hash of the file content, hex-encoded.

source_id.description: ID of the source the file was imported from. `null` for uploaded files.

updated_at.description: When the file record last changed, ISO 8601. `null` when it has not changed since creation.

version.description: Always `1` for this file ID. A content update, including a source sync, creates a different file ID rather than incrementing this value. This is separate from the document's content revision. Send it as `expectedRevision` to [Delete Document File](/en/api-reference/documents-and-chunks/delete-document-file).

active_operations.description: Operations under way in the current phase, such as `parse`, `chunk`, `embedding`, or `publication`.

completed_at.description: When the task ended, ISO 8601. `null` while it runs.

created_at.description: When the task was created, ISO 8601. [Get Indexing Task](/en/api-reference/indexing-tasks/get-indexing-task) reports the same task's times in epoch milliseconds.

error_message.description: The message for `error_code`. Can differ from `failure.message`.

failure.description: Error details when `state` is `failed`. `stage` is the `phase` the task failed in, and `traceId` is the task ID. `null` otherwise.

id.description: Indexing task ID. The same ID works with [Get Indexing Task](/en/api-reference/indexing-tasks/get-indexing-task), [Cancel Indexing Task](/en/api-reference/indexing-tasks/cancel-indexing-task), and [Retry Indexing Task](/en/api-reference/indexing-tasks/retry-indexing-task).

knowledge_space_id.description: Internal ID of the knowledge base. Not the knowledge base ID in the path.

phase.description: What the task is doing: `queued`, `parsing`, `outline_summary`, `chunking_indexing`, `graph_admission`, `publication`, or `complete`.

retry_at.description: When the automatic retry runs, ISO 8601. Set while `state` is `retry_wait`.

semantic_enrichment.description: Knowledge graph building status for the indexed content. Deep and Research searches follow the knowledge graph. When building wasn't scheduled, `state` is `not_scheduled` while the task runs and `disabled` once it has ended.

stage.description: Last checkpoint reached, in forward order: `queued`, `parsed`, `outline_built`, `nodes_generated`, `projection_built`, `smoke_eval_passed`, `published`. It stays at the last checkpoint when the task fails or is canceled, so read `state` for the outcome.

state.description:
Run state:

- `dispatch_pending`, `queued`: waiting for a worker.
- `retry_wait`: an automatic retry is scheduled at `retry_at`.
- `running`: a worker is indexing.
- `succeeded`: the revision is published and serves queries. `semantic_enrichment` can still be running.
- `failed`: see `failure`. Restart it with [Retry Indexing Task](/en/api-reference/indexing-tasks/retry-indexing-task).
- `canceled`.
- `superseded`: a newer attempt replaced this one.

`succeeded`, `failed`, `canceled`, and `superseded` are terminal.

updated_at.description: When the task or its enrichment last changed, ISO 8601.

activated_at.description: When the revision became active, ISO 8601. `null` for a revision that never became active.

content_hash.description: SHA-256 hash of the content, hex-encoded.

created_at.description: When the revision was created, ISO 8601.

document_asset_id.description: ID of the document file behind this revision. Use it with [Get Document File](/en/api-reference/documents-and-chunks/get-document-file).

document_asset_version.description: The document file's `version` when this revision was created.

knowledge_space_id.description: Internal ID of the knowledge base. Not the knowledge base ID in the path.

mime_type.description: MIME type of the document file.

revision.description: Revision number, starting at `1`. The `revision` path value for [List Chunks](/en/api-reference/documents-and-chunks/list-chunks).

size_bytes.description: Size of the document file in bytes.

state.description: `candidate` while the revision is being indexed, `active` for the revision the knowledge base serves, `superseded` after a newer revision became active, `failed` when indexing failed.

action.description: Suggested next step, when there is one: `configure_model`, `configure_parser`, `configure_source`, `contact_admin`, `reupload`, or `retry`. `null` when not applicable; omitted from HTTP error bodies.

code.description: Stable error code in upper snake case, for example `KNOWLEDGE_FS_CONFLICT` or `SOURCE_CREDENTIAL_TEST_FAILED`.

message.description: Public message for the error code or failure category. Provider error details are not exposed.

parameters.description: Up to 8 values that qualify the failure, with keys among `attempt`, `currentRowVersion`, `documentCount`, `expectedRowVersion`, `fileSizeBytes`, `limit`, `maxFileSizeBytes`, `maxItems`, `modelType`, `providerKind`, `retryAfterSeconds`, and `status`. `null` when there are none; omitted from HTTP error bodies.

retryPolicy.description: Whether a retry can help: `automatic` (the service retries on its own), `manual` (retry yourself), `after_configuration` (fix the knowledge base's setup in Dify first), or `never` (change the request).

stage.description: Stage the failure belongs to, for example `query_generation` or `credential-test`. `null` when not applicable; omitted from HTTP error bodies.

traceId.description: Reference to quote when contacting an administrator. May be `null` in a successful response containing failure details, or omitted from an HTTP error body.

base_head_revision.description: Internal. Not needed to follow the task.

candidate_fingerprint.description: Internal. Not needed to follow the task.

candidate_publication_id.description: Internal. Not needed to follow the task.

completed_at.description: When the task reached a terminal stage, in epoch milliseconds. `null` while it runs and after a retry.

created_at.description: When the task was created, in epoch milliseconds.

document_asset_id.description: ID of the document file being indexed. Usable with [Get Document File](/en/api-reference/documents-and-chunks/get-document-file). It is the `asset.id` of the [Re-index Documents](/en/api-reference/documents-and-chunks/re-index-documents) item that started the task, even when you submitted a document ID.

error.description: Short failure message. Can differ from `failure.message`. Set only when `stage` or `run_state` is `failed`. Otherwise `null`, including on canceled tasks.

execution_attempts.description: Attempts made so far. [Retry Indexing Task](/en/api-reference/indexing-tasks/retry-indexing-task) resets it to `0`, so repeated retries never exhaust the attempt budget on their own.

failure.description: Error details when the task failed. `null` otherwise.

knowledge_space_id.description: Internal ID of the knowledge base. Not the knowledge base ID in the path.

max_execution_attempts.description: Attempts allowed before the task fails.

run_state.description:
Scheduler state of the current attempt:

- `dispatch_pending`: accepted, waiting to be dispatched to a worker.
- `queued`: dispatched, waiting for a worker.
- `running`: a worker is executing the task.
- `retry_wait`: an automatic retry is scheduled, and `stage` stays unchanged.
- `succeeded`: accompanies `stage: published`.
- `failed`, `canceled`: terminal.
- `superseded`: a newer attempt replaced this one. Terminal, reported with `stage: canceled`, and accepted by neither cancel nor retry.

`null` when not set. [Retry Indexing Task](/en/api-reference/indexing-tasks/retry-indexing-task) sets it to `dispatch_pending`.

stage.description:
Indexing stage, in forward order:

- `queued`
- `parsed`
- `outline_built`
- `nodes_generated`
- `projection_built`
- `smoke_eval_passed`
- `published`

`published` means the new revision is active. `failed` and `canceled` are the other terminal values. [Retry Indexing Task](/en/api-reference/indexing-tasks/retry-indexing-task) keeps the checkpoint the attempt had reached, so the value is rarely `queued` after a retry.

updated_at.description: When the task last changed, in epoch milliseconds.

version.description: Version of the document file being indexed.

KnowledgeBaseOutlineHeading.description: Offsets refer to the parsed document text. They are not positions in the original file.

end_offset.description: Zero-based UTF-8 byte offset in the parsed document text. Exclusive end. `null` when unknown.

end_page.description: Last page of the section, starting at `1`. `null` when the file has no pages.

metadata.description: Additional heading details. Free-form object.

section_path.description: Headings from the document root to this heading, itself included.

source_element_ids.description: IDs of the parsed elements the heading was detected from.

source_node_ids.description: Internal. Not needed to read the outline.

start_offset.description: Zero-based UTF-8 byte offset in the parsed document text. Inclusive start. `null` when unknown.

start_page.description: First page of the section, starting at `1`. `null` when the file has no pages.

summary.description: Generated summary of the section. `null` when none was generated.

title_location.description: Where the heading sits in the file. `null` when unknown.

toc_source.description: How the heading was detected: `native-toc`, `llm-inferred`, `parser-heading`, or `fallback`.

data.description: Entries of this page, in the order the run recorded them.

metadata.description: Details of the entry. The available keys depend on the view. In the missing-chunks view, `metadata` also carries the missing item's own metadata keys.

availability.description: `available`, or `unavailable` when the chunk was deleted or is no longer readable.

citationCount.description: Chunks view: number of citations on the chunk.

conflictCount.description: Chunks view: number of conflicts recorded on the chunk. `0` when the chunk is unavailable.

documentId.description: Chunks view: document file ID of the primary citation. Usable with [Get Document File](/en/api-reference/documents-and-chunks/get-document-file). Present only when the chunk has a citation.

documentVersion.description: Chunks view: version of that document file. Present only when the chunk has a citation.

freshness.description: Chunks view. How current the chunk was at retrieval time.

observedAt.description: When the chunk was last observed, ISO 8601. Present when known.

sourceUpdatedAt.description: When the source last changed, ISO 8601. Present when known.

status.description: `fresh`, `stale`, or `unknown`.

nodeId.description: Conflicts view: ID of the chunk that holds the conflict.

reason.description:
Conflicts view: free-text explanation of the conflict. Missing-chunks view: why the chunk was not used, one of `not-retrieved`, `permission-filtered`, `stale`, `conflict`, or `unknown`.

`permission-filtered`: An access check excluded the chunk.

score.description: Chunks view: relevance score of the chunk, from 0 to 1.

scores.description: Chunks view: score breakdown, each from 0 to 1.

rerank.description: Rerank score. Present when a reranker ran.

sectionPath.description: Chunks view: heading path of the primary citation, outermost first. Present only when the chunk has a citation.

severity.description: Conflicts view: `info`, `warning`, or `blocking`. `blocking` conflicts are the ones that keep the run from answering.

text.description: Chunks view. Text of the chunk. A placeholder when the chunk is unavailable.

title.description: Chunks view: last element of `sectionPath`. Present only when `sectionPath` is not empty.

unavailableReason.description: Why the chunk is unavailable, for example `evidence-unavailable`. Present only when `availability` is `unavailable`.

name.description: Entry name. Chunks view: the chunk ID. Conflicts view: `conflict-<n>`, numbered from 1 within the chunk. Missing-chunks view: `missing-<n>`, numbered from 1.

path.description: Internal path of the entry. Informational. This API does not serve it.

resource_type.description: `node` in the chunks and conflicts views, `evidence` in the missing-chunks view.

target_id.description:
The entry's target:

- Chunks view: the chunk ID.
- Conflicts view: the chunk it conflicts with, or its own chunk ID when none is recorded.
- Missing-chunks view: the expected chunk ID when recorded, else the entry `name`.

May not resolve to a live chunk when `metadata.availability` is `unavailable`.

next_cursor.description: Cursor for the next page, or `null` on the last page. Send it back as `cursor`.

path.description: Internal path of the view, for example `/queries/<query_record_id>/evidence`. Informational. This API does not serve it.

truncated.description: `true` when more entries exist beyond this page. Follow `next_cursor` to read them.

budget_usd.description: Spend ceiling from the request in USD. `null` when none was set.

completed_at.description: When the task reached `completed`, `failed`, or `canceled`, in epoch milliseconds. `null` while the task is running.

budgetExceeded.description: `true` when spend crossed `budgetUsd` and the task was canceled for that reason. Absent otherwise.

budgetUsd.description: The request's `budgetUsd`. Absent when no budget was set.

entries.description: One entry per recorded model call, oldest first.

costUsd.description: Cost of the call in USD.

provider.description: Model provider that served the call.

recordedAt.description: Epoch milliseconds when the cost was recorded.

step.description: Step that made the call: `pageindex.layer`, `pageindex.semantic`, `pageindex.whole-tree`, `research.judge`, `research.plan`, `graph.plan`, `query.answer`, or `query.image-expand`.

usage.description: Token usage of the call: `promptTokens`, `completionTokens`, `totalTokens`, `estimated`, `reserved`, `status` (`reserved`, `succeeded`, or `failed`), and `researchModelCallId`. A reservation for a call still in flight is an entry too, and counts toward `totalUsd`.

totalUsd.description: Sum of `entries[].costUsd` in USD. `0` until the first model call is recorded.

created_at.description: Epoch milliseconds when the task was created.

error.description:
Failure code, the same value as `failure.code`. Present only when `stage` is `failed`, and `null` otherwise, including for canceled tasks.

On a failed research task, `failure.code` is one of `RESEARCH_TASK_CAPABILITY_REVOKED`, `RESEARCH_TASK_DISPATCH_DEAD`, `RESEARCH_TASK_EXECUTION_ATTEMPTS_EXHAUSTED`, `RESEARCH_TASK_FAILED`, `RESEARCH_TASK_PERMISSION_SNAPSHOT_INVALID`, or `RESEARCH_TASK_RUNTIME_SNAPSHOT_INVALID`.

failure.description:
Error details. Present only when `stage` is `failed`, and `null` otherwise. Members without a value are `null` here. `traceId` is the task ID.

When `action` is `retry`, create a new task with [Create Research Task](/en/api-reference/research-tasks/create-research-task).

action.description: Suggested next step, when there is one: `configure_model`, `configure_parser`, `configure_source`, `contact_admin`, `reupload`, or `retry`. `null` when not applicable.

code.description: Research-task failure code, matching this task's `error`.

message.description: Public message for the task failure. Provider error details are not exposed.

parameters.description: Up to 8 values that qualify the failure, with keys among `attempt`, `currentRowVersion`, `documentCount`, `expectedRowVersion`, `fileSizeBytes`, `limit`, `maxFileSizeBytes`, `maxItems`, `modelType`, `providerKind`, `retryAfterSeconds`, and `status`. `null` when there are none.

retryPolicy.description: Whether a retry can help: `automatic` (the service retries on its own), `manual` (retry yourself), `after_configuration` (fix the knowledge base's setup in Dify first), or `never` (change the request).

traceId.description: Research task ID. Quote it when contacting an administrator.

id.description: Research task ID. Use it as `research_task_id` in the task operations.

knowledge_space_id.description: Internal ID of the knowledge base. Not the knowledge base ID in the path.

limits.description: Limits from the request, with snake_case keys. `null` when the request carried no `limits`. A member that was not sent is `null`. Convert the keys back to camelCase before sending them to [Create Research Task](/en/api-reference/research-tasks/create-research-task) again.

metadata.description: The `metadata` object sent at creation, without keys that start with `__knowledgeFs`.

mode.description: Retrieval depth of the task: `fast`, `deep`, or `research`.

query_images.description: Images used in the original query. Omitted for text-only queries.

upload_file_id.description: ID of the image file used in the original query.

stage.description:
Where the task is in its lifecycle. Tasks move forward one stage at a time:

- `queued`: accepted, waiting for a worker.
- `planning`: resolving the retrieval plan.
- `retrieving`: searching the knowledge base. A retrieval checkpoint may be written.
- `analyzing`: reading and weighing the retrieved chunks.
- `generating`: writing the answer. The final result is written during this stage.
- `completed`: finished. Read its results with [List Research Task Results](/en/api-reference/research-tasks/list-research-task-results).
- `failed`: stopped with an error. See `error` and `failure`.
- `canceled`: stopped by [Cancel Research Task](/en/api-reference/research-tasks/cancel-research-task) or by the budget.
- `paused`: The task is paused. Check any failure details with the deployment operator, or cancel it.

`completed`, `failed`, and `canceled` are terminal.

top_k.description: Maximum number of chunks kept after the search results are merged and reranked: the request's `topK`, or the knowledge base's **TOP K** when omitted.

updated_at.description: Epoch milliseconds of the last update to the task record, including internal checkpoints and retry scheduling.

error_message.description: The message for `error_code`. Can differ from `failure.message`.

nodes_completed.description: Knowledge graph nodes built: `0` until `state` is `ready`, then the same as `nodes_total`.

nodes_total.description: Knowledge graph nodes to build. `null` until known.

provider_calls_maximum.description: Most model calls knowledge graph building may make.

state.description: `not_scheduled`, `pending`, `running`, `ready`, `failed`, or `disabled`. Knowledge graph building can still be `pending` or `running` after the indexing task has published its revision.

updated_at.description: When the enrichment last changed, ISO 8601.

active_profile_available.description: `true` when both an embedding model and retrieval settings are live, which happens after the first document is indexed.

active_profile_revisions.description: Revisions of the live models. Each is `null` until the first document is indexed. Once a profile is active, a change through [Update Knowledge Base Settings](/en/api-reference/settings/update-knowledge-base-settings) runs as a migration.

embedding.description: Revision of the live embedding model.

retrieval.description: Revision of the live retrieval settings.

capabilities.description:
Readiness of the published settings. Three flags stand for retrieval depths, with `query` standing for `fast`.

To check readiness for a specific depth, send that depth explicitly as `mode` and check its flag. Do not use a pending `retrieval.default_mode` to identify the depth of a query that omits `mode`.

index.description: Documents can be indexed. The models are live.

ingest.description: Documents can be added. The models are live, or complete pending settings are ready to be activated by the first document.

source_sync.description: Sources can sync. Same condition as `ingest`.

configuration_state.description: `active` when an embedding model and complete retrieval settings (with an enabled rerank model) are stored. `setup-required` when either is missing. `validation-failed` when the pending settings failed validation while the first document was indexed. `issues` names the settings that failed.

embedding.description:
Embedding model. The pending selection when one is stored, otherwise the live model. A pending selection can differ from the model queries use now. `null` when none is set.

Its `dimension`, `revision`, and `vector_space_id` are informational, and no operation takes them.

dimension.description: Vector dimension, observed when the model is first used. `null` until the model is live.

plugin_id.description: Plugin that provides the model, as `organization/plugin_name`.

revision.description: Revision of the live embedding model. `null` until the model is live.

vector_space_id.description: Identifies where the model's vectors are stored. `null` until the model is live.

issues.description: What keeps the knowledge base from being ready. Empty when nothing does.

code.description:
What is wrong with the setting:

- `missing`: the selection is absent, or rerank is disabled.
- `validation_failed`, `unavailable`, or `incompatible`: the pending settings failed validation. For `incompatible`, check the model's supported task, embedding dimension, and whether the provider returned the selected model.
- `binding_missing`: the published content is not ready to use the configured models. Check indexing progress in Dify.
- `unavailable` on `publication`: the published content is not ready for every depth.

field.description: The setting concerned: `embedding`, `reasoning`, `rerank`, or `publication` (the published content).

retryable.description: Whether waiting and retrying can clear the issue without a settings change.

retrieval.description: Retrieval settings. The pending selection when one is stored, otherwise the live settings. A pending selection can differ from the settings queries use now. `null` when none is set.

default_mode.description: Default depth in the returned retrieval settings: `fast`, `deep`, or `research`. When a query omits `mode`, it uses the published default, which can differ from this value if pending settings are returned.

reasoning_model.description: System reasoning model. Its `dimension`, `revision`, and `vector_space_id` are always `null`.

plugin_id.description: Plugin that provides the model, as `organization/plugin_name`.

rerank.description: Rerank model. Its `model` object uses the camelCase key `pluginId`, unlike the rest of this response.

model.description: Rerank model selection. `null` when no rerank model is set.

pluginId.description: Plugin that provides the model, as `organization/plugin_name`.

revision.description: Revision of the live retrieval settings. `null` while the settings are pending.

score_threshold.description: Score cutoff that drops low-scoring chunks.

stage.description: Where the cutoff applies. `mode-final` applies it to the final score of the depth that runs: the rerank score at `fast` and `deep`, the PageIndex score at `research`. `rerank` is the same thing under its old name.

value.description: The cutoff score, 0 to 1. `null` when not set.

top_k.description: Maximum number of chunks each search returns.

revision.description: Settings revision. Send it as `expectedRevision` in [Update Knowledge Base Settings](/en/api-reference/settings/update-knowledge-base-settings). The other revision fields in this response are not that value.

candidate_publication_fingerprint.description: Internal. Not needed to follow the migration.

completed_at.description: When the migration ended (`succeeded`, `failed`, or `canceled`), ISO 8601. `null` while it runs.

error_code.description: Code of the last failure, for example `PROFILE_MIGRATION_ATTEMPTS_EXHAUSTED` or `VECTOR_SPACE_QUOTA_EXCEEDED`. `null` when none.

evaluation_summary.description: Flat map of evaluation results recorded for the rebuilt index. `null` when none was recorded.

id.description: Migration ID. Pass it to [Get Settings Migration](/en/api-reference/settings/get-settings-migration).

knowledge_space_id.description: Internal ID of the knowledge base. Not the knowledge base ID in the path.

rebuild_scope.description:
What the migration rebuilds:

- `full-vector-space`: an embedding model change re-embeds every document.
- `full-page-index-summary-outline`: a reasoning model change rebuilds the page index, summaries, and outlines.
- `clone-publication`: any other retrieval change reuses the current index.

run_state.description:
Progress of the migration:

- `queued`, `running`: in progress.
- `succeeded`: the new settings are in effect.
- `failed`: stopped. `error_code` says why. Check the models in [Get Knowledge Base Settings](/en/api-reference/settings/get-knowledge-base-settings) before trying the change again.
- `canceled`: a newer change of the same kind replaced this migration before it finished. Follow the newer one.

updated_at.description: When the migration last changed, ISO 8601.

connection_id.description: Connection the source uses for credentials. Pass it as `connectionId` when binding another source to the same connection. `null` when unbound.

credential_configured.description: `true` when the source holds a credential reference of its own. `null` when it holds none, as with sources bound to a connection.

knowledge_space_id.description: Internal ID of the knowledge base. Not the knowledge base ID in the path.

last_synced_at.description: Completion time of the latest completed sync (`completed` or `zero_results`) or completed import. Set by [List Sources](/en/api-reference/sources/list-sources) only. `null` elsewhere and when the source has never synced.

metadata.description: Provider settings and server-managed sync or page-selection data. May include provider identifiers and `parameters`; connection-managed settings need not appear here. Credential-like keys are removed. Do not copy the entire object when creating another source.

permission_scope.description: Content scopes required to read this source. An empty list adds no content restriction within the knowledge base. Knowledge base authorization still applies.

status.description:
`active`, `syncing`, `error`, or `disabled`. Most operations return the stored value. [List Sources](/en/api-reference/sources/list-sources) derives it from the latest sync run:

- `failed` or `canceled` run: `error`
- `completed` or `zero_results` run: `active`
- Any live run: `syncing`

`disabled` is never overridden.

sync_policy.description: The source's sync schedule. Set by [List Sources](/en/api-reference/sources/list-sources) only. `null` elsewhere and when no schedule exists. Read it on its own with [Get Sync Policy](/en/api-reference/sources/get-sync-policy) and change it with [Update Sync Policy](/en/api-reference/sources/update-sync-policy).

sync_workflow.description:
The source's active sync or import run (`crawl-import`, `online-document-import`, or `online-drive-import`), or else its latest sync run. [List Sources](/en/api-reference/sources/list-sources) sets it when a run is active or newer than the source. [Update Source](/en/api-reference/sources/update-source) sets it when the call started a sync. `null` otherwise. Crawl previews and imports from them never appear here.

To follow one run, call [Get Source Run](/en/api-reference/source-syncs-and-imports/get-source-run) with its `id`.

type.description:
`web` (website crawl), `connector` (online document or online drive), `upload`, or `object-storage`.

For a `connector` source, `metadata.providerKind` is `online-document` or `online-drive`. For a `web` source it is `website`.

Dify fills `upload` and `object-storage` sources.

updated_at.description: Last change, ISO 8601.

uri.description: Crawl root URL for `web` sources. `connector://<connection_id>` for Dify-created connector sources.

version.description: Source version, increased on every write. Send it as `expectedVersion` on [Update Source](/en/api-reference/sources/update-source), as `expectedRevision` on [Delete Source](/en/api-reference/sources/delete-source), and as `expectedSourceVersion` on [Update Sync Policy](/en/api-reference/sources/update-sync-policy).

auth_kind.description: How the connection authenticates. `endpoint` for connections Dify manages.

checkpoint.description: Last step the run reached: `queued`, `provider-read`, `preview-staged`, `selection-frozen`, `materialized`, `cleanup-staging`, or `source-committed`. [Retry Source Run](/en/api-reference/source-syncs-and-imports/retry-source-run) starts the run over whatever its checkpoint.

id.description: Run ID. Pass it to [Get Source Run](/en/api-reference/source-syncs-and-imports/get-source-run), [Cancel Source Run](/en/api-reference/source-syncs-and-imports/cancel-source-run), or [Retry Source Run](/en/api-reference/source-syncs-and-imports/retry-source-run).

kind.description:
What the run does:

- `sync`: started by [Sync Source](/en/api-reference/source-syncs-and-imports/sync-source), [Update Source](/en/api-reference/sources/update-source), a schedule, or Dify.
- `crawl-preview`: started by [Preview Website Crawl](/en/api-reference/source-syncs-and-imports/preview-website-crawl). It keeps this kind while [Import Selected Pages](/en/api-reference/source-syncs-and-imports/import-selected-pages) imports from it.
- `crawl-import`: started by [Import Website Pages](/en/api-reference/source-syncs-and-imports/import-website-pages).
- `online-document-import`, `online-drive-import`: started by [Import Source Items](/en/api-reference/source-syncs-and-imports/import-source-items).

Dify also starts previews and imports when a source is added or edited there.

knowledge_space_id.description: Internal ID of the knowledge base. Not the knowledge base ID in the path.

max_execution_attempts.description: Limit on `execution_attempts`. Once it is reached, [Retry Source Run](/en/api-reference/source-syncs-and-imports/retry-source-run) answers `409`.

progress_completed.description: Items finished, including unchanged items a sync checked.

progress_failed.description: Always `0` for source runs: a failing item fails the whole run.

progress_total.description:
Items the run expects to process: the pages or items an import requested, the pages a crawl preview has staged so far, or the source's items once a sync has listed them. `null` until known.

While an [Import Website Pages](/en/api-reference/source-syncs-and-imports/import-website-pages) run crawls its URLs, `progress_completed` and `progress_total` both count the pages crawled so far. Once every URL is crawled, they restart at `0` of the number of URLs.

state.description:
Progress of the run.

Live states:

- `queued`: waiting for a worker
- `crawling`: a crawl preview is fetching pages
- `preview_ready`: a crawl preview is waiting for [Import Selected Pages](/en/api-reference/source-syncs-and-imports/import-selected-pages) or [Cancel Source Run](/en/api-reference/source-syncs-and-imports/cancel-source-run)
- `importing`: importing and indexing items
- `syncing`: refreshing the source's documents

Terminal states:

- `completed`: every item was imported or refreshed, indexed, and made active
- `zero_results`: a crawl preview found no pages
- `failed`: see `failure`
- `canceled`

After `failed` or `canceled`, [Retry Source Run](/en/api-reference/source-syncs-and-imports/retry-source-run) runs it again, and [Sync Source](/en/api-reference/source-syncs-and-imports/sync-source) starts a new sync.

updated_at.description: Last change, ISO 8601. Also moves when a scheduled sync starts.

schema.description:
A stream of Server-Sent Events. Parse it per the [SSE Streaming guide](/en/api-reference/guides/streaming): read `data:` lines, dispatch on the `event` field, skip `ping` (keep-alive; a Chatflow stream opens with one, then more arrive roughly every 10 seconds).

**Events by app type** (the reply events, then how the stream closes):

- **Chatbot**: `message` chunks (concatenate in order) → `message_end`.
- **Legacy Agent**: `agent_thought` reasoning and tool-call steps alongside `agent_message` chunks → `message_end`.
- **Agent**: `agent_message` chunks with `agent_thought` steps alongside → one closing `message` carrying the complete answer (treat it as the final answer, not extra text to append) → `message_end`. Its `message_end` metadata carries `usage` (plus `annotation_reply` on an annotation match) and never `retriever_resources`.
- **Chatflow**: `workflow_started` → node events (`node_started`, `node_finished`, plus iteration and loop variants) alongside `message` chunks → then, by outcome:
  - **Success**: `message_end`, then `workflow_finished`
  - **Failure**: `workflow_finished` with status `failed`, then `error`; no `message_end`
  - **Pause**: `human_input_required`, then `workflow_paused` (the stream ends here; the run resumes separately)

**Add-ons**:

- Text-to-speech auto-play: `tts_message` audio chunks interleave, and `tts_message_end` trails the closing event.
- Chatflow LLM nodes with `reasoning_format: separated` also emit `reasoning_chunk` deltas carrying the model's reasoning.

**Common fields**: apart from `ping`, every event includes `conversation_id`, `message_id`, and `created_at` (Unix epoch seconds); all but `error` also include `task_id`. Workflow, node, and human-input events (Chatflow apps) nest their payload under `data` and, except for `agent_log`, carry a top-level `workflow_run_id`.

**Reply events**

| Event | App | Fires on | Key fields |
|:---|:---|:---|:---|
| `message` | Chatbot, Chatflow, Agent | each answer chunk (concatenate in order); for Agent, one closing chunk with the complete answer | `answer` |
| `agent_message` | Legacy Agent, Agent | each answer chunk (concatenate in order) | `answer` |
| `agent_thought` | Legacy Agent, Agent | each reasoning or tool-call step | `position`, `thought`, `tool`, `tool_input` (JSON), `observation`, `message_files` |
| `message_replace` | All | output moderation replaces the answer so far | `answer`; Chatflow also `reason` |
| `reasoning_chunk` | Chatflow | each reasoning-content delta, when an LLM node uses `reasoning_format: separated` (concatenate in order; a final `is_final: true` event marks reasoning finished and may carry an empty `reasoning`) | `data.message_id`, `data.reasoning`, `data.node_id`, `data.is_final` |
| `message_file` | Chatbot, Legacy Agent | the assistant returns a file | `type`, `belongs_to`, `url` |
| `message_end` | All | the answer is complete | `metadata` (`usage`, `retriever_resources`) |
| `tts_message`, `tts_message_end` | Chatbot, Legacy Agent, Chatflow | audio chunk / end, when TTS auto-play is on | `audio` |

**Workflow and node events** (Chatflow apps only)

Each event nests its payload under a `data` object.

| Event | Fires on | Key `data` fields |
|:---|:---|:---|
| `workflow_started` | the run begins | `inputs` |
| `node_started` | a node begins | `node_id`, `node_type`, `title` |
| `node_finished` | a node ends | `status`, `outputs`, `execution_metadata` |
| `node_retry` | a node retries after a failure | `retry_index` |
| `iteration_started`, `iteration_next`, `iteration_completed` | Iteration node progress (informational) | `data` |
| `loop_started`, `loop_next`, `loop_completed` | Loop node progress (informational) | `data` |
| `agent_log` | an Agent node step log (informational; no `workflow_run_id`) | `data` |
| `workflow_finished` | the run ends | `status` (`succeeded`, `failed`, `partial-succeeded`, `stopped`), `outputs`, `total_tokens` |
| `workflow_paused` | the run pauses | `paused_nodes`, `reasons` |
| `human_input_required` | the run reaches a Human Input node | `form_token`, `form_content`, `expiration_time` |

After a pause this stream ends at `workflow_paused`. Submit the form via [Submit Human Input Form](/en/api-reference/human-input/submit-human-input-form) or let it time out; the resumed run, including `human_input_form_filled`/`human_input_form_timeout` through `workflow_finished`, streams from [Stream Workflow Events](/en/api-reference/workflow-runs/stream-workflow-events).

**Transport events**

| Event | Fires on | Key fields |
|:---|:---|:---|
| `error` | a failure ends the stream; HTTP stays `200` | `status` (e.g. `400`), `code` (e.g. `invalid_param`), `message` |
| `ping` | keep-alive; opens every Chatflow stream, then roughly every 10 seconds | none |

post.description:
**Available for**: Chatflow, Workflow, Agent, Chatbot, Legacy Agent, Text Generator apps.

Uploads a file and returns its `id` for later requests to reference. The file belongs to the uploading end user: only requests carrying the same `user` can reference it.

Which file types an app actually consumes depends on its file-upload settings; read them from [Get App Parameters](/en/api-reference/applications/get-app-parameters).

file.description:
The file to upload, as one `multipart/form-data` part. The filename must not contain `/` or `\`.

Any extension is accepted unless it is on the deployment's security blacklist (`UPLOAD_FILE_EXTENSION_BLACKLIST`, empty by default).

Size limits per category: images 10 MB, audio 50 MB, video 100 MB, other files 15 MB by default (Dify Cloud uses the defaults). Self-hosted deployments adjust them with the `UPLOAD_*_FILE_SIZE_LIMIT` [environment variables](/en/self-host/deploy/configuration/environments).

user.description: End-user identifier this upload belongs to, defined by your app and unique within it. Omit it to attribute the upload to the shared `DEFAULT-USER`. Only later requests with the same `user` can reference the file. See [End User Identity](/en/api-reference/guides/end-user-identity).

post.description:
Runs the query that [Create Query Token](/en/api-reference/queries/create-query-token) issued a token for and streams the answer as Server-Sent Events. The credential is the query token, not the knowledge base API key. The token is checked when the request is accepted.

For the two-call flow and how to read the stream, see [Query the Knowledge Base](/en/api-reference/guides/knowledge-base#query-the-knowledge-base).

For which errors to retry and what the error details mean, see [Handle Errors](/en/api-reference/guides/knowledge-base#handle-errors).

A successful query saves its query record before sending `answer.done`. Repeating the call runs the query again.

parameters.description: The `trace_id` from the [Create Query Token](/en/api-reference/queries/create-query-token) response, the same value as the token's `trace_id` claim. A value that does not match the token is rejected with `403`. See [Query the Knowledge Base](/en/api-reference/guides/knowledge-base#query-the-knowledge-base).

knowledgeSpaceId.description: Internal ID of the knowledge base, copied from the `request` object of [Create Query Token](/en/api-reference/queries/create-query-token). Must match the token. A mismatch is rejected with `403`.

mode.description: Retrieval depth, copied from the `request` object of [Create Query Token](/en/api-reference/queries/create-query-token). `null` is accepted and means the knowledge base's default depth.

query.description: The question. Use a nonblank query. Also limited to 16,384 UTF-8 bytes.

Send the `request` object from [Create Query Token](/en/api-reference/queries/create-query-token) unchanged. Unknown fields answer `400`.

Optional fields marked nullable treat `null` as omitted.

The normalized request must fit within 65,536 UTF-8 bytes. Exceeding this budget answers `413`. See [Request Size Limits](/en/api-reference/guides/knowledge-base#request-size-limits).

schema.description:
Each frame has an `event:` line naming the event and a `data:` line holding one JSON object. Dispatch on the `event:` line; the JSON carries no `event` field.

Set your client's read timeout to allow for your slowest retrieval mode. The API has no read timeout of its own and sends no keep-alive events. For work that must survive a client timeout, use [Create Research Task](/en/api-reference/research-tasks/create-research-task).

See [Query the Knowledge Base](/en/api-reference/guides/knowledge-base#query-the-knowledge-base) for the streaming flow.

**Events**

- `answer.delta`: one piece of the answer.
  - `delta`: the text to append.
  - `traceId`: the query record ID.
- `answer.done`: the answer is complete and its query record is saved.
  - `finishReason`: `retrieval-evidence` when chunks were found, `no-retrieval-evidence` when nothing matched.
  - `metadata`: an open map. It carries `mode` and `evidenceBundle` at `fast`, `deep`, and `research` depth, `citations` with `retrieval-evidence`, and other keys the run produced. `evidenceBundle.items` holds the retrieved chunks with their text and scores.

    To inspect them later, call [List Query Chunks](/en/api-reference/query-records/list-query-chunks). It returns them page by page and marks chunks whose document has since been deleted.
  - `traceId`: the query record ID.
- `answer.error`: the query failed after the stream opened.
  - `code`: the failure, one of:
    - `RETRIEVAL_EXECUTION_LEASE_LOST`: the knowledge base entered deletion, or the run expired. Run the query again.
    - `KNOWLEDGE_FS_UNAVAILABLE`: any other failure while generating the answer or saving the query record.
  - `error`: the message.
  - `failure`: error details: `category`, `code`, `message`, `retryPolicy`, `stage`, `traceId`, and optionally `action`.
    - `stage`: always `query_generation`.
  - `traceId`: the query record ID.

**`citations`**

One entry per retrieved chunk that supports the answer:

- `nodeId`: the chunk ID.
- `label`: `node:<nodeId>`.
- `documentAssetId`: the document file the chunk came from.
- `sectionPath`: the outline path.
- `pageNumber`: page number, starting at 1, when the source provides page information. Omitted otherwise.
- `projectionIds`: IDs of the search indexes that contributed to this match. Use `documentAssetId` to identify the source file.
- `sources`: which searches found the chunk: `dense`, `fts`, `pageindex`, or `visual`.

An image citation can include `multimodalCandidate.assetRef.analysisUnavailable.reason`. When present, image analysis was skipped because of a resource limit or an image-processing failure. Related text can still contribute to the result.

`evidenceBundle.items[].citations[]` may also carry `startOffset` and `endOffset`. These are zero-based UTF-8 byte offsets into the parsed document text, with an inclusive start and exclusive end. Use the returned chunk text to display a citation; do not slice the original file at these offsets.

**Closing sequence by outcome**

- Success: zero or more `answer.delta`, then one `answer.done`, then the stream closes.
- Failure: `answer.error` in place of `answer.done`, then the stream closes. Pieces already delivered may precede it, and the HTTP status stays `200`. Treat it as final and start a new query to try again.
- Client disconnect. The run is canceled and the stream ends.

**Answer content**: at `fast` and `deep`, one `answer.delta` carries a digest of the retrieved chunks (`Retrieval evidence answer:` followed by numbered section paths and their text). At `research`, the synthesized answer streams as one or more pieces. When nothing matched, the single piece is `I could not find evidence for that query in the indexed retrieval projections.` and `finishReason` is `no-retrieval-evidence`.

Answers are capped at 2,000 characters at every depth. Reaching that length does not tell you whether the answer was truncated.

A successful run:

```text
event: answer.delta
data: {"delta":"Retrieval evidence answer:\n1. Policies / Refunds: Refund window extended from 14 to 30 days for annual plans.","traceId":"6c1f0b2e-9d3a-4f5b-8c7d-0e1f2a3b4c5d"}

event: answer.done
data: {"finishReason":"retrieval-evidence","metadata":{"mode":"fast","generator":"hybrid-query","topScore":0.83,"citations":[{"documentAssetId":"b3f4c8d2-6a1e-4f7b-9c0d-2e3f4a5b6c7d","label":"node:9f2e6b41-7c3d-4a58-b0e9-1d2c3f4a5b6e","nodeId":"9f2e6b41-7c3d-4a58-b0e9-1d2c3f4a5b6e","pageNumber":4,"projectionIds":["c7a0d5b2-3e14-4f89-a6b7-0c1d2e3f4a5b"],"sectionPath":["Policies","Refunds"],"sources":["dense","fts"]}],"evidenceBundle":{"createdAt":"2026-09-06T08:31:12Z","id":"e4b2f7a0-1c3d-4e58-9f6a-0b1c2d3e4f5a","items":[{"citations":[{"documentAssetId":"b3f4c8d2-6a1e-4f7b-9c0d-2e3f4a5b6c7d","documentVersion":1,"pageNumber":4,"sectionPath":["Policies","Refunds"]}],"conflicts":[],"freshness":{"status":"fresh"},"metadata":{},"nodeId":"9f2e6b41-7c3d-4a58-b0e9-1d2c3f4a5b6e","score":0.83,"scores":{"final":0.83,"retrieval":0.71},"text":"Refund window extended from 14 to 30 days for annual plans."}],"missingEvidence":[],"query":"What changed in the refund policy this quarter?","state":"answerable","traceId":"6c1f0b2e-9d3a-4f5b-8c7d-0e1f2a3b4c5d"}},"traceId":"6c1f0b2e-9d3a-4f5b-8c7d-0e1f2a3b4c5d"}

```

Failure after the stream opened:

```text
event: answer.error
data: {"code":"KNOWLEDGE_FS_UNAVAILABLE","error":"Agent Knowledge Base is temporarily unavailable. Try again later.","failure":{"action":"retry","category":"dependency","code":"KNOWLEDGE_FS_UNAVAILABLE","message":"Agent Knowledge Base is temporarily unavailable. Try again later.","retryPolicy":"manual","stage":"query_generation","traceId":"6c1f0b2e-9d3a-4f5b-8c7d-0e1f2a3b4c5d"},"traceId":"6c1f0b2e-9d3a-4f5b-8c7d-0e1f2a3b4c5d"}

```

status.description:
Aggregate state:

- `running`: at least one item is still in progress.
- `completed`: every item completed (reached at least `projection_built`, which comes before `published`) or was reported as `not_found`.
- `failed`: every item is terminal and at least one failed.
- `canceled`: every item is terminal, none failed, and at least one was canceled.

`completed` does not guarantee that the new revisions are active yet. When that matters, check each task with [Get Indexing Task](/en/api-reference/indexing-tasks/get-indexing-task) for `stage: published`, using the task IDs you kept from [Re-index Documents](/en/api-reference/documents-and-chunks/re-index-documents).

Returns a [Delete Document Files in Batch](/en/api-reference/documents-and-chunks/delete-document-files-in-batch) request with each file's outcome and the current state of each accepted file's deletion job. Only the API key that sent the batch can read it.

The batch is done when every entry in `results` is `rejected` or its `job.run_state` is `completed` or `failed`. Reading the batch never moves a `pending` file forward. Files left `pending` weren't accepted when the batch stopped partway. To retry them, send the original request again with the same `Idempotency-Key`.

For the deletion flow, see [Delete Documents and Sources](/en/api-reference/guides/knowledge-base#delete-documents-and-sources).

get.description:
Returns the progress of a deletion requested with [Delete Document File](/en/api-reference/documents-and-chunks/delete-document-file) or [Delete Source](/en/api-reference/sources/delete-source), or of one file in [Delete Document Files in Batch](/en/api-reference/documents-and-chunks/delete-document-files-in-batch). Poll it until `run_state` is `completed` or `failed`.

Only the API key that requested the deletion can read its job. The job stays readable after the deletion completes.

[Get Document File](/en/api-reference/documents-and-chunks/get-document-file) or [Get Source](/en/api-reference/sources/get-source) answers `404` for the deleted object from the moment the deletion is accepted. When a source is deleted with `documents=keep`, its documents are hidden while the job runs and come back when it completes, with `source_id` set to `null`. If the job fails, they stay hidden.

A failed deletion cannot be retried over this API.

For the deletion flow, see [Delete Documents and Sources](/en/api-reference/guides/knowledge-base#delete-documents-and-sources).

delete.description:
Requests the deletion of up to 100 document files in one call and reports an outcome for each file. As with [Delete Document File](/en/api-reference/documents-and-chunks/delete-document-file), avoid files of active revisions.

Send the JSON body with this `DELETE`. If your client omits bodies on DELETE requests, configure it to send the body explicitly.

Files are sorted by `documentId`, then `expectedRevision`, and each is handled on its own. A file that does not exist, has a stale `expectedRevision`, is already being deleted, or cannot be deleted with this key comes back in `results` as `rejected`, and the other files proceed. An infrastructure failure stops the run and leaves the remaining files `pending`.

To continue after an infrastructure failure, or after the call fails as a whole, send the same request again with the same `Idempotency-Key`. It returns the original batch with the jobs already accepted and retries only the `pending` files.

This call creates no bulk task.

For the deletion flow, see [Delete Documents and Sources](/en/api-reference/guides/knowledge-base#delete-documents-and-sources).

parameters.description: Knowledge base ID: the last segment of the Service API endpoint shown in the knowledge base's **API Access** dialog (`…/knowledge-fs/spaces/<knowledge base ID>`), and the segment after `/datasets/new/` in the address bar.
parameters.name: knowledge_base_id

parameters.description: Required identifier for this deletion request. Repeating the same key and request with the same API key returns the original batch and retries its `pending` files. Reusing the key for a different request, or from another API key, answers `409`. Use printable ASCII characters without leading or trailing whitespace.
parameters.name: Idempotency-Key

documents.description: Files to delete. Each `documentId` must appear once. A larger batch answers `400`. The deployment may set a lower cap.

expectedRevision.description: The document file's current `version`, from [List Document Files](/en/api-reference/documents-and-chunks/list-document-files) or [Get Document File](/en/api-reference/documents-and-chunks/get-document-file). A document file's `version` is always `1`. Not the revision number from [List Document Revisions](/en/api-reference/documents-and-chunks/list-document-revisions).

requestBody.description: The normalized request must fit within 1,048,576 UTF-8 bytes. See [Request Size Limits](/en/api-reference/guides/knowledge-base#request-size-limits).

202.description:
The batch was recorded. `results` gives each file's outcome, and `items` lists the accepted files. Deletion runs in the background. [Get Document File](/en/api-reference/documents-and-chunks/get-document-file) answers `404` from the moment a file's deletion is accepted. To follow every file to the end, poll [Get Deletion Batch](/en/api-reference/deletion-jobs/get-deletion-batch) (the batch `status_url`).

Poll the returned job IDs. To retry files left `pending`, send the same request again with the same `Idempotency-Key`.

Location.description: The same URL as the batch `status_url`.

post.description:
Queues an indexing task to rebuild each selected document's index from its current file. Returns a bulk task ID to follow the tasks together.

Exactly one of `all: true` or `documentIds` must be given.

No file is re-uploaded. Follow each task with [Get Indexing Task](/en/api-reference/indexing-tasks/get-indexing-task) using `compilation_job.id`, and the whole request with [Get Bulk Task](/en/api-reference/indexing-tasks/get-bulk-task).

For the re-index flow, see [Re-index and Track Indexing](/en/api-reference/guides/knowledge-base#track-indexing).

parameters.description: Knowledge base ID: the last segment of the Service API endpoint shown in the knowledge base's **API Access** dialog (`…/knowledge-fs/spaces/<knowledge base ID>`), and the segment after `/datasets/new/` in the address bar.
parameters.name: knowledge_base_id

parameters.description:
Send a key on every call. It makes the call safe to retry. Use 8 to 255 printable ASCII characters without leading or trailing whitespace; a malformed key answers `400`.

Repeating the same key and body returns the original bulk task instead of starting new indexing tasks. Reusing the key with a different body, from another API key, in another knowledge base, or for another operation answers `409`.
parameters.name: Idempotency-Key

schema.description: Send `all: true` or a nonempty `documentIds` array, but not both. With `documentIds`, `all` may be omitted, `false`, or `null`. With `all: true`, `documentIds` may be omitted or `null`; an empty array is rejected.

all.description: Set to `true` to re-index every document file the key can read. When there are more than the cap (100 by default), the call answers `400` and nothing is re-indexed.

documentIds.description: Documents to re-index, by document ID (from [List Documents](/en/api-reference/documents-and-chunks/list-documents)) or by document file ID (from [List Document Files](/en/api-reference/documents-and-chunks/list-document-files)). The deployment may set a lower cap. Duplicate IDs are collapsed, so `total` can be smaller than the number sent. Send each ID once, and `items` lines up with your request in order.

requestBody.description:
Optional fields marked nullable treat `null` as omitted.

The normalized request must fit within 1,048,576 UTF-8 bytes. See [Request Size Limits](/en/api-reference/guides/knowledge-base#request-size-limits).

bulk_job_id.description: Bulk task ID. Poll it with [Get Bulk Task](/en/api-reference/indexing-tasks/get-bulk-task).

items.description: One entry per distinct ID sent, in request order, followed by one entry per selected file when `all` is `true`. IDs that resolve to the same document file share one entry.

asset.description: The document file being re-indexed. `null` unless `status` is `queued`.

id.description: Indexing task ID. Poll it with [Get Indexing Task](/en/api-reference/indexing-tasks/get-indexing-task).

document_id.description: The ID as sent, or the document file ID for items selected by `all: true`. Set when `status` is `disabled`, `not_found`, `failed`, or `pending`. `null` for `queued` items, whose document file ID is `asset.id`.

error.description: Failure message when `status` is `failed`. `null` otherwise.

status.description:
- `queued`: an indexing task was started, and `asset`, `compilation_job`, and `status_url` are set.
- `disabled`: the document is disabled, so nothing was queued, and the bulk task counts it as canceled. No operation in this API enables a document.
- `not_found`: no readable document file matched the ID.
- `failed`: no indexing task was started. `code` and `error` say why.
- `pending`: it could not be confirmed whether an indexing task was started.

status_url.description: Internal path of the task. Informational. Follow the task with [Get Bulk Task](/en/api-reference/indexing-tasks/get-bulk-task) instead. `null` unless `status` is `queued`.

delete.description:
Requests the deletion of a document file and returns the deletion job. Every revision built on the file stops returning chunks through [List Chunks](/en/api-reference/documents-and-chunks/list-chunks).

Avoid deleting the file of a document's active revision. The document is left `failed` with no active revision and drops out of [List Documents](/en/api-reference/documents-and-chunks/list-documents) and Dify's document list. It still counts toward the document quota.

Send the JSON body with this `DELETE`. If your client omits bodies on DELETE requests, configure it to send the body explicitly.

For the deletion flow, see [Delete Documents and Sources](/en/api-reference/guides/knowledge-base#delete-documents-and-sources).

A stale value answers `409` and nothing is deleted.

patch.description:
Merges keys into a document's `user_metadata` and returns the updated document. Unlike the other operations on this path, it takes the document ID, not a document file ID.

Send the document's `row_version` as `expectedRowVersion`. Read the document right before updating it, and on `409` read it again and resend.

parameters.description: Knowledge base ID: the last segment of the Service API endpoint shown in the knowledge base's **API Access** dialog (`…/knowledge-fs/spaces/<knowledge base ID>`), and the segment after `/datasets/new/` in the address bar.
parameters.name: knowledge_base_id

parameters.description: The document ID: `id` from [List Documents](/en/api-reference/documents-and-chunks/list-documents) or [Get Document](/en/api-reference/documents-and-chunks/get-document), or `document_id` from [Get Document by File](/en/api-reference/documents-and-chunks/get-document-by-file). Not a document file ID, even though [Get Document File](/en/api-reference/documents-and-chunks/get-document-file) and [Delete Document File](/en/api-reference/documents-and-chunks/delete-document-file) take one on this path. A document file ID answers `404`.
parameters.name: document_file_id

expectedRowVersion.description: The document's current `row_version`, from [Get Document](/en/api-reference/documents-and-chunks/get-document) or [List Documents](/en/api-reference/documents-and-chunks/list-documents), or the `row_version` this operation last returned. A newly active revision and enabling or disabling the document in Dify also change it, so read it right before updating. A stale value answers `409` and nothing changes.

patch.description:
Keys to merge into `user_metadata`:

- A key with a value sets that key.
- A key with `null` removes it.
- Keys you leave out stay as they are.

Each key names a metadata field, in lowercase snake case. The field must already exist: create it in Dify first. The value must match the field's type: a string for `string`, a finite number for `number`, and a UTC timestamp such as `2026-12-01T00:00:00Z` for `time`.

Reserved keys answer `400`: `activeRevision`, `contentHash`, `documentAssetId`, `documentAssetVersion`, `mimeType`, `provenance`, `providerItemId`, `sourceId`, `system`, `systemMetadata`, `tenantId`, `__knowledgeFs`, and keys starting with `system.`, `provenance.`, or `__knowledgeFs.`.

requestBody.description: The normalized request must fit within 131,072 UTF-8 bytes. See [Request Size Limits](/en/api-reference/guides/knowledge-base#request-size-limits).

200.description: The updated document. Its `row_version` is the value to send on the next update, and `latest_task` is always `null` in this response.

get.description:
Returns the heading tree built for the current version of a document file.

The outline exists only after indexing has built it, and not at all for a file whose indexing failed before that step. After a re-index, this operation returns the outline the new indexing task built, once that task publishes.

The response is not paginated.

parameters.description: Document file ID. From [List Document Files](/en/api-reference/documents-and-chunks/list-document-files).

created_at.description: When the outline was built, ISO 8601.

document_asset_id.description: ID of the document file the outline was built for.

knowledge_space_id.description: Internal ID of the knowledge base. Not the knowledge base ID in the path.

metadata.description: Additional outline details. Free-form object.

nodes.description: Top-level headings, in document order. Nested headings are in each heading's `children`.

outline_version.description: Internal. Not needed to read the outline.

parse_artifact_id.description: Internal. Not needed to read the outline.

updated_at.description: When the outline last changed, ISO 8601. `null` when it has not changed since it was built.

version.description: The document file's `version` the outline belongs to. It does not change when a re-index rebuilds the outline, because a document file's `version` never changes.

post.description:
Restarts an indexing task whose `run_state` is `failed` or `canceled` under the same task ID and returns the updated task. Poll [Get Indexing Task](/en/api-reference/indexing-tasks/get-indexing-task) with the same ID afterwards.

To index the document again once the task is `published`, use [Re-index Documents](/en/api-reference/documents-and-chunks/re-index-documents). For the re-index flow, see [Re-index and Track Indexing](/en/api-reference/guides/knowledge-base#track-indexing).

An attempt with `run_state: superseded` cannot be retried, even though its `stage` is `canceled`. If you saved a newer task ID from a re-index response, poll that task.

ID of a query session, as a UUID. Omit it to start a new session. [Run Query](/en/api-reference/queries/run-query) returns the session ID in its `x-session-id` response header.

post.description: Creates a research task for a question and returns it with `stage` `queued`. The task then runs in the background. For the plan, create, poll, and read flow, see [Run a Research Task](/en/api-reference/guides/knowledge-base#run-a-research-task).

parameters.description: Knowledge base ID: the last segment of the Service API endpoint shown in the knowledge base's **API Access** dialog (`…/knowledge-fs/spaces/<knowledge base ID>`), and the segment after `/datasets/new/` in the address bar.

parameters.description:
Optional key that makes creation safe to retry. Use 8 to 255 printable ASCII characters without leading or trailing whitespace; a malformed key answers `400`.

Repeating the same key and body with the same API key returns the original task, in its current state, with `202` instead of creating another. Keys are unique within the workspace: reusing a key with a different body, from another API key, in another knowledge base, or for another operation answers `409`.
parameters.name: Idempotency-Key

value.query: What changed in the 2025 refund policy, and which regions are affected?

budgetUsd.description:
Spend ceiling in USD. Enforced while the task runs, not at creation. The task is accepted even when the [Plan Research Task](/en/api-reference/research-tasks/plan-research-task) estimate exceeds it. Before each model call, the task checks the call's worst-case cost against the budget, and it is canceled instead of making a call that could pass the budget.

A call can still cost more than its worst-case estimate, so `cost.totalUsd` can end above `budgetUsd`. A budget cancellation before the `generating` stage leaves the task with no answer. Worst-case costs usually run well above the plan's estimates, so when you need an answer, set the ceiling well above `estimates.costUsd.max`, and higher still for a large `topK`.

A task stopped by its budget ends in stage `canceled`.

limits.description:
Checked once, at creation, against the plan's estimates. A task whose estimates exceed a limit is rejected with `422`. Omitting `limits` skips these checks. Use `budgetUsd` to bound spending while the task runs.

An estimate equal to its limit passes. Size these against the `estimates` from [Plan Research Task](/en/api-reference/research-tasks/plan-research-task).

metadata.description:
Free-form object stored with the task and returned as `metadata`. Keys that start with `__knowledgeFs` are reserved and dropped.

Include a unique value such as `client_request_id` to recognize the task if the creation response is lost. This helps you find the task. To make a retry return the original task instead of creating another, send `Idempotency-Key`.

mode.description: Retrieval depth: `fast`, `deep`, or `research` (see [Retrieval Depth](/en/cloud/use-dify/knowledge-base/retrieval-settings#retrieval-depth)). Omit it to use the knowledge base's default depth, `retrieval.default_mode` in [Get Knowledge Base Settings](/en/api-reference/settings/get-knowledge-base-settings).

query.description: The question. Use a nonblank query. Also limited to 16,384 UTF-8 bytes.

topK.description: Maximum number of chunks kept after the search results are merged and reranked. Explicit values must be between 1 and 50. If omitted, uses the knowledge base's published **TOP K** setting, which can be up to 100. Higher values give the model more context and more noise. Lower values stay focused and can miss relevant chunks.

requestBody.description:
Optional fields marked nullable treat `null` as omitted.

The normalized request must fit within 65,536 UTF-8 bytes. See [Request Size Limits](/en/api-reference/guides/knowledge-base#request-size-limits).

value.query: What changed in the 2025 refund policy, and which regions are affected?

202.description: The task was accepted. `stage` is `queued`, `mode` is the resolved depth, and `cost.totalUsd` is `0`. A repeat with the same `Idempotency-Key` and body returns the original task in its current state.

mode.description: Retrieval depth: `fast`, `deep`, or `research` (see [Retrieval Depth](/en/cloud/use-dify/knowledge-base/retrieval-settings#retrieval-depth)). value.query: What changed in the 2025 refund policy, and which regions are affected?

budget.description: Verdict of the cost estimate against the request's `budgetUsd`.

budget_usd.description: The request's `budgetUsd`. `null` when none was sent.

exceeds_budget.description: `true` when `estimates.costUsd.estimated` is above `budgetUsd`. Always `false` without a budget. Advisory only: [Create Research Task](/en/api-reference/research-tasks/create-research-task) still accepts the task and cancels it when its next model call could pass the budget.

remaining_budget_usd.description: `budgetUsd` minus the estimated cost. Negative when over budget. `null` without a budget.

estimates.description: Work, cost, and latency estimates for the task. Compare them with the `limits` you intend to send to [Create Research Task](/en/api-reference/research-tasks/create-research-task).

cacheHitProbability.description: Estimated share of retrieval served from cache, from `0` to `1`.

inputTokens.description: Estimated model input tokens across all steps.

latencyMs.description: Estimated end-to-end duration in milliseconds. Time the first poll of [Get Research Task](/en/api-reference/research-tasks/get-research-task) from `p50`.

p95.description: 95th-percentile estimate. This is the value checked against `limits.timeoutMs`.

outputTokens.description: Estimated model output tokens across all steps.

scannedResources.description: Estimated documents and sections read. Checked against `limits.maxScannedResources`.

workBounds.description: Ranges behind the point estimates. [Create Research Task](/en/api-reference/research-tasks/create-research-task) checks the point estimates, not these ranges.

modelCalls.description: Estimated, minimum, and maximum number of model calls.

openedResources.description: Estimated, minimum, and maximum number of documents and sections opened.

retrievalSteps.description: Estimated, minimum, and maximum number of retrieval rounds.

knowledge_space_id.description: Internal ID of the knowledge base. Not the knowledge base ID in the path.

query.description: The question with surrounding whitespace removed.

retrieval_plan.description: How the search would be run.

fusion_limit.description: Candidates kept after merging vector and keyword results.

query_language.description: Detected language of the question: `cjk`, `latin`, `mixed-cjk-latin`, or `other`.

requested_mode.description: The `mode` from the request, or the knowledge base's default depth when omitted: `fast`, `deep`, or `research`.

rerank_candidate_limit.description: Candidates passed to the rerank model.

resolved_mode.description: The depth that would run: `fast`, `deep`, or `research`. Send the same `mode` to [Create Research Task](/en/api-reference/research-tasks/create-research-task). A different depth there checks your `limits` against different estimates.

strategy_version.description: Version of the retrieval strategy that built this plan.

top_k.description: Maximum number of chunks kept after the search results are merged and reranked.

estimatedCostUsd.description: Estimated cost of the step in USD.

name.description: Step name. `plan`, `retrieve`, `analyze`, and `generate` always appear, in that order. `inspect` follows `plan` when the retrieval strategy reads document outlines.
