evidence_bundle.description:
Retrieved chunks the task had collected when this result was written.

An item whose document file was deleted after retrieval comes back as a placeholder:

- `text` is `Evidence deleted or unavailable`.
- `citations[]` keep only `documentAssetId`, `documentVersion`, and an empty `sectionPath`.
- `conflicts` is empty.
- `freshness.status` is `unknown`.
- `metadata.traceEvidenceAvailability` is `{"status": "unavailable", "reason": "document-deleted-or-unavailable"}`.

createdAt.description: ISO 8601 timestamp when the bundle was written.

id.description: ID of this bundle of retrieved chunks.

items.description: Retrieved chunks with their scores and citations, best first.

citations.description: Where the chunk comes from. At least one per item.

items.description: Offsets refer to the parsed document text. They are not positions in the original file or the answer.

artifactHash.description: SHA-256 of the document file the citation points to. Absent when not recorded.

documentAssetId.description: Document file ID. Read the file's name with [Get Document File](/en/api-reference/documents-and-chunks/get-document-file). To find its document, pass it with `documentVersion` to [Get Document by File](/en/api-reference/documents-and-chunks/get-document-by-file).

documentVersion.description: The document file's `version` at retrieval time.

endOffset.description: Zero-based UTF-8 byte offset in the parsed document text. Exclusive end. Omitted when unavailable.

pageNumber.description: Page number, starting at 1, when the source provides page information. Omitted otherwise.

sectionPath.description: Section headings from the document root to the cited section.

startOffset.description: Zero-based UTF-8 byte offset in the parsed document text. Inclusive start. Omitted when unavailable.

conflicts.description: Disagreements between this chunk and other retrieved chunks. Empty when none.

withNodeId.description: `nodeId` of the chunk this one conflicts with. Absent when the conflict is not tied to one chunk.

freshness.description: How current the cited content is.

observedAt.description: ISO 8601 timestamp when the content was last seen. Absent when unknown.

sourceUpdatedAt.description: ISO 8601 timestamp of the source's last update. Absent when unknown.

status.description: `fresh`, `stale`, or `unknown`.

metadata.description: Additional item details. Carries `traceEvidenceAvailability` on placeholder items.

score.description: Overall relevance from `0` to `1`. The same value as `scores.final`.

freshness.description: Score for how recent the source is. Absent when not computed.

rerank.description: Score from the rerank model. Absent when reranking did not run.

retrieval.description: Score from vector and keyword search.

missingEvidence.description: Chunks the run expected but could not use. Empty when none.

expectedEvidenceId.description: ID of the expected chunk, when known.

metadata.description: Additional details.

retrievalQuery.description: The query text actually sent to retrieval when it differs from `query`. Absent otherwise.

state.description: How well the retrieved chunks support an answer: `partial` (the retrieval checkpoint, before analysis runs), `answerable`, `not-enough-evidence`, `conflict` (sources disagree), or `permission-limited` (permissions kept some chunks out).

traceId.description: ID of the run that produced the bundle, when one was recorded. A research task is not recorded as a query record, so [Get Query Record](/en/api-reference/query-records/get-query-record) does not take this ID.

knowledge_space_id.description: Internal ID of the knowledge base. Not the knowledge base ID in the path.

sequence.description: Position of the result within the task, starting at `1`.

next_cursor.description: Cursor for the next page, or `null` on the last page. Send it back as `cursor`.

patch.description:
Changes the knowledge base's embedding model or retrieval settings. For setting models before and after content is indexed, see [Change Models or Retrieval Settings](/en/api-reference/guides/knowledge-base#change-models-or-retrieval-settings).

What happens depends on whether models are active yet:

- Before the first document is indexed, the settings are stored as pending, and the call answers `200`. They are validated and take effect when the first document is indexed. Omitting `embedding` or `retrieval` leaves that group at its pending value.
- Once models are active, the call returns `202` and the change runs as a migration. An embedding or reasoning model change rebuilds the content it affects, while other retrieval changes take effect without a rebuild. Poll [Get Settings Migration](/en/api-reference/settings/get-settings-migration) with `migration.id` until it ends, then read the final settings. A change that needs no migration, such as resending the active embedding model, returns `200`.

Rules:

- Send at least one of `embedding` or `retrieval`. Once models are active, send only one of them per call.
- `retrieval` cannot be stored without an enabled rerank model, so send `rerank.enabled: true` and a `rerank.model` with it.
- `retrieval` needs an embedding model, sent in the same call or stored earlier. Otherwise the call answers `409`.
- `scoreThreshold.enabled: true` requires a `scoreThreshold.value`.

parameters.description: Knowledge base ID: the last segment of the Service API endpoint shown in the knowledge base's **API Access** dialog (`…/knowledge-fs/spaces/<knowledge base ID>`), and the segment after `/datasets/new/` in the address bar.
parameters.name: knowledge_base_id

request.summary: Request Example - Before models are active

request_embedding.summary: Request Example - Change the embedding model

embedding.description:
The embedding model used to index content. Once a model is active, changing it starts a migration that re-embeds every document.

Find the values with [Get Available Models](/en/api-reference/models/get-available-models): `text-embedding` for embedding models, `llm` for the reasoning model, `rerank` for rerank models.

`pluginId` is the plugin's `organization/plugin_name`, `provider` its provider name, `model` the model name.

Get Available Models returns one `provider` string shaped `organization/plugin_name/provider_name`, so `langgenius/openai/openai` splits into `pluginId` `langgenius/openai` and `provider` `openai`. A bare `openai` stands for `langgenius/openai/openai`.

model.description: Model name as the provider plugin lists it, for example `text-embedding-3-small`.

pluginId.description: Plugin that provides the model, as `organization/plugin_name` (for example `langgenius/openai`).

provider.description: Provider name inside the plugin, for example `openai`.

expectedRevision.description: The current `revision` from [Get Knowledge Base Settings](/en/api-reference/settings/get-knowledge-base-settings). A stale value answers `409` and nothing changes.

retrieval.description: The retrieval settings a query uses: reasoning model, rerank model, score threshold, `topK`, and the depth to fall back on.

defaultMode.description: Retrieval depth used when a query omits `mode`. See [Retrieval Depth](/en/cloud/use-dify/knowledge-base/retrieval-settings#retrieval-depth).

reasoningModel.description: System reasoning model: used during indexing and by `research` queries. Find the values with [Get Available Models](/en/api-reference/models/get-available-models).

model.description: Model name as the provider plugin lists it.

pluginId.description: Plugin that provides the model, as `organization/plugin_name`.

rerank.description:
The rerank model applied to retrieved chunks.

This operation requires `enabled: true` and a non-null model.

model.description: Rerank model selection. Find the values with [Get Available Models](/en/api-reference/models/get-available-models).
Model name as the provider plugin lists it.

pluginId.description: Plugin that provides the model, as `organization/plugin_name`.

scoreThreshold.description: Score cutoff that drops low-scoring chunks.

enabled.description: Whether the cutoff applies. When `true`, send `value`.

stage.description: Where the cutoff applies. `mode-final` applies it to the final score of the depth that runs: the rerank score at `fast` and `deep`, the PageIndex score at `research`. `rerank` is the same thing under its old name.

value.description: The cutoff score. Chunks scoring below it are dropped. Higher cutoffs keep only close matches and risk returning nothing. Lower cutoffs let broader matches through.

topK.description: Maximum number of chunks each search returns. Higher values give the model more context and more noise. Lower values stay focused and can miss relevant chunks.

requestBody.description:
[Get Knowledge Base Settings](/en/api-reference/settings/get-knowledge-base-settings) answers in snake_case and this body is camelCase, so its response cannot be sent back unchanged.

Optional fields marked nullable treat `null` as omitted.

The normalized request must fit within 65,536 UTF-8 bytes. See [Request Size Limits](/en/api-reference/guides/knowledge-base#request-size-limits).

200.description: No migration started: the settings were stored as pending, or models are active and the change needed no migration. `settings` has the same shape as [Get Knowledge Base Settings](/en/api-reference/settings/get-knowledge-base-settings), and its `revision` is the value to send on the next update. While the settings are pending, `active_profile_available` stays `false` and `capabilities.query` stays `false`.

migration.description: The migration this change started. Follow it with [Get Settings Migration](/en/api-reference/settings/get-settings-migration).

202.description: The change started a migration, described in `migration`. `settings` has the same shape as [Get Knowledge Base Settings](/en/api-reference/settings/get-knowledge-base-settings).

get.description:
Lists the connections of this knowledge base, oldest first. Pass a connection's `id` as `connectionId` to [Create Source](/en/api-reference/sources/create-source) to add a source that reads through it.

The list holds a connection only after a source from that provider has been added to the knowledge base in Dify. To use a new provider, add its first source in Dify. For the steps to add a source, see [Add a Source](/en/api-reference/guides/knowledge-base#add-a-source).

get.description:
Returns one source run. Use it to follow any run by ID, including crawl previews and imports from them, which [List Sources](/en/api-reference/sources/list-sources) does not show.

A run that ends `completed` has imported or refreshed every item, indexed it, and made it active. The run waits up to 10 minutes for each document's indexing, and a document that takes longer fails it.

After `failed`, read `failure`, then call [Retry Source Run](/en/api-reference/source-syncs-and-imports/retry-source-run) or start a new run with a new `Idempotency-Key`.

For how to follow, retry, and cancel runs, see [Follow Source Runs](/en/api-reference/guides/knowledge-base#follow-source-runs).

post.description:
Cancels a source run that has not finished and returns it.

A canceled run stops before it updates the source's page list. Items it finished stay until the next sync, which removes any not on the page list. Documents of items left out of an import aren't deleted, unless the cancel came while they were being removed.

A run that already ended `completed`, `zero_results`, or `canceled` comes back unchanged.

For how to follow, retry, and cancel runs, see [Follow Source Runs](/en/api-reference/guides/knowledge-base#follow-source-runs).

post.description:
Runs a `failed` or `canceled` source run again from the start, under the same run ID, and returns it queued. Progress is reset, so an import fetches every item again and a sync starts over. A crawl preview whose pages were already selected imports them again without crawling.

To repeat a canceled crawl preview or a failed [Import Website Pages](/en/api-reference/source-syncs-and-imports/import-website-pages) run, don't retry it: start a new preview or import with a new `Idempotency-Key`.

No request body.

For how to follow, retry, and cancel runs, see [Follow Source Runs](/en/api-reference/guides/knowledge-base#follow-source-runs).

post.description:
Imports pages from a crawl preview into documents and returns the same run, now queued to import. Poll [Get Source Run](/en/api-reference/source-syncs-and-imports/get-source-run) with the same `id` until `state` is `completed`, `failed`, or `canceled`.

The pages are imported from what the preview staged, without crawling again.

When the run completes, these pages become the source's page list. Each import sets the whole list, so include every page you want the source to keep.

For the preview-and-import flow, see [Import Website Pages](/en/api-reference/guides/knowledge-base#import-website-pages).

post.description:
Adds a source that reads through an existing connection, found with [List Source Connections](/en/api-reference/sources/list-source-connections). Nothing is crawled or imported.

Repeating a successful creation creates another source. Add a unique `metadata.client_request_id` and keep it until you receive the source ID.

To fill the source, call [Preview Website Crawl](/en/api-reference/source-syncs-and-imports/preview-website-crawl) or [Import Website Pages](/en/api-reference/source-syncs-and-imports/import-website-pages) for a `web` source, or [Import Source Items](/en/api-reference/source-syncs-and-imports/import-source-items) for a `connector` source. For the steps, see [Add a Source](/en/api-reference/guides/knowledge-base#add-a-source).

parameters.description: Knowledge base ID: the last segment of the Service API endpoint shown in the knowledge base's **API Access** dialog (`…/knowledge-fs/spaces/<knowledge base ID>`), and the segment after `/datasets/new/` in the address bar.
parameters.name: knowledge_base_id

connectionId.description: Connection that supplies the credentials the source reads with. It must belong to this knowledge base and be `active`. From `id` of [List Source Connections](/en/api-reference/sources/list-source-connections).

metadata.description:
Provider settings and your own non-sensitive metadata. Add a unique `client_request_id` to recognize this source if the creation response is lost. It is returned with the source, but the API does not enforce uniqueness or deduplicate requests.

Set `providerKind` to the connection's `configuration.providerKind`, and pick the source `type` that fits it. Settings that come from the connection may be absent from the source response.

If you build `metadata` from an existing source's response, leave out fields starting with `__knowledgeFs`, `credentials`, and the `parameters` object. `credentialId`, when present, refers to a credential Dify holds.

permissionScope.description: Leave empty or omit. Only an empty list is accepted.

status.description: `disabled` pauses scheduled syncs.

type.description: Send `web` for a website crawl, or `connector` for an online document or online drive provider (set `metadata.providerKind`). `upload` and `object-storage` are for sources Dify fills.

uri.description: Crawl root URL for `web`. `connector://<connectionId>` for `connector`, matching what Dify writes.

requestBody.description:
Optional fields marked nullable treat `null` as omitted.

The normalized request must fit within 262,144 UTF-8 bytes. See [Request Size Limits](/en/api-reference/guides/knowledge-base#request-size-limits).

delete.description:
Requests deletion of a source and returns the deletion job.

For what happens to a deleted source's documents, see [Delete Documents and Sources](/en/api-reference/guides/knowledge-base#delete-documents-and-sources).

parameters.description: Knowledge base ID: the last segment of the Service API endpoint shown in the knowledge base's **API Access** dialog (`…/knowledge-fs/spaces/<knowledge base ID>`), and the segment after `/datasets/new/` in the address bar.

parameters.description: Source ID. From [List Sources](/en/api-reference/sources/list-sources).

parameters.description: Required identifier for this deletion request. Repeating the same key and request with the same API key returns the original job with `202`. Reusing the key for a different request, or from another API key, answers `409`. Use printable ASCII characters without leading or trailing whitespace.

parameters.description:
`cascade` also deletes the documents the source produced. `keep` keeps them: they are hidden while the deletion job runs and come back when it completes, with `source_id` set to `null` and no longer refreshed.

Before deleting with `keep`, save the IDs of files with this `source_id` from [List Document Files](/en/api-reference/documents-and-chunks/list-document-files): their `source_id` becomes `null` once the deletion completes.

expectedRevision.description: The source's current `version` from [List Sources](/en/api-reference/sources/list-sources) or [Get Source](/en/api-reference/sources/get-source). A stale value answers `409` and nothing changes.

job.description: The deletion job. `target_type` is `source`, and `mode` echoes `documents`.

status_url.description: URL of the deletion job in this API: absolute when the deployment sets `SERVICE_API_URL`, otherwise a path that starts with `/v1/`. The same value is sent in the `Location` response header.

202.description:
Deletion accepted. `job` describes the background deletion.

[Get Source](/en/api-reference/sources/get-source) answers `404` from the moment the deletion is accepted. To confirm that it finished, poll [Get Deletion Job](/en/api-reference/deletion-jobs/get-deletion-job) (the `status_url`) until `run_state` is `completed` or `failed`.

patch.description:
Updates a source's name, status, URI, metadata, or provider parameters, and can start a sync when the configuration changed.

Send at least one of `name`, `status`, `uri`, `metadata`, or `providerParameters`. `expectedVersion` and `syncAfterUpdate` alone are rejected.

For how to start and follow a sync, see [Sync and Schedule Sources](/en/api-reference/guides/knowledge-base#sync-and-schedule-sources).

parameters.description: Knowledge base ID: the last segment of the Service API endpoint shown in the knowledge base's **API Access** dialog (`…/knowledge-fs/spaces/<knowledge base ID>`), and the segment after `/datasets/new/` in the address bar.
parameters.name: knowledge_base_id

parameters.description: Source ID. From [List Sources](/en/api-reference/sources/list-sources).
parameters.name: source_id

schema.description: Supply at least one non-null `metadata`, `name`, `providerParameters`, `status`, or `uri`. `expectedVersion` and `syncAfterUpdate` alone do not make an update.

expectedVersion.description: The source's current `version` from [List Sources](/en/api-reference/sources/list-sources) or [Get Source](/en/api-reference/sources/get-source). A stale value answers `409` and nothing changes. Omit it to let the last write win.

metadata.description:
Keys to merge into the stored metadata. Nested objects merge; arrays are replaced.

Must not contain `parameters` (use `providerParameters`) or credentials. `datasource`, `pluginId`, `provider`, `providerId`, and `providerKind` cannot change. `tenantId` is overwritten by the service.

providerParameters.description:
Parameters defined by the selected data source. This replaces the entire stored `metadata.parameters` object, so include every value you need to keep. Values are booleans, finite numbers, or strings. Credential-like keys are rejected.

If [Get Source](/en/api-reference/sources/get-source) does not expose the complete non-sensitive parameters and you do not already know the data source's parameter contract, configure the source in Dify instead.

status.description:
New status. Set `active` or `disabled`. `error` and `syncing` are set by sync runs.

`disabled` prevents new scheduled syncs and prevents this update from starting a sync. It does not cancel a sync that was already accepted.

syncAfterUpdate.description:
When `true`, asks for a sync run after the write. The response carries the run as `sync_workflow`, or `sync_workflow: null` when the call started none.

A sync starts only when this call changes `uri`, `providerParameters`, or a `metadata` value, and the source's `status` is not `disabled`. Re-sending the current values does not start a sync. To sync without changing the source, call [Sync Source](/en/api-reference/source-syncs-and-imports/sync-source).

For a website source with a saved page list, sync refreshes those pages. Change the list with [Import Website Pages](/en/api-reference/source-syncs-and-imports/import-website-pages) or [Import Selected Pages](/en/api-reference/source-syncs-and-imports/import-selected-pages).

uri.description: New URI. For `web` sources it must be an HTTP or HTTPS URL without embedded credentials. `metadata.parameters.url` is updated to match.

requestBody.description:
Optional fields marked nullable treat `null` as omitted.

The normalized request must fit within 262,144 UTF-8 bytes. See [Request Size Limits](/en/api-reference/guides/knowledge-base#request-size-limits).

post.description:
Starts a sync of a source now and returns the run. Poll [Get Source Run](/en/api-reference/source-syncs-and-imports/get-source-run) with its `id` until `state` is `completed`, `failed`, or `canceled`.

What a sync does depends on the source type:

- `web`: re-crawls the pages in the source's page list and re-indexes those that changed. A source with no page list yet re-crawls the whole site and imports the pages it finds.

  Documents whose page no longer comes back are deleted, unless the source's `metadata.remoteDeletionPolicy` is `retain`.
- `connector`: refreshes the items the source imported.
- `upload` and `object-storage`: the run completes without changes.

A `disabled` source can be synced this way: `disabled` stops only scheduled syncs.

A source runs one sync, preview, or import at a time. Wait for its active run to end before starting another, and cancel a crawl preview you won't import.

For how to start and follow a sync, see [Sync and Schedule Sources](/en/api-reference/guides/knowledge-base#sync-and-schedule-sources).

Saving does not start a sync. The first scheduled sync is due one interval after the update, and each later one an interval after the previous one was queued. To sync now, call [Sync Source](/en/api-reference/source-syncs-and-imports/sync-source).

post.description:
Imports online document pages or online drive files into a connector source and returns the run. Poll [Get Source Run](/en/api-reference/source-syncs-and-imports/get-source-run) with its `id` until `state` is `completed`, `failed`, or `canceled`.

The items replace the source's documents: once they are imported, documents of the source's items not in `items` are deleted. Send every item you want the source to keep.

After a source's first completed import, an import can name only items from that import. A new item fails the run with `SOURCE_OPERATION_FAILED`, which retrying does not fix: add new items to the source in Dify.

The source must be a `connector` source, and `kind` must match its `metadata.providerKind`. A source runs one sync, preview, or import at a time, so wait for its active run to end first.

For the browse-and-import flow, see [Import Online Documents and Drive Files](/en/api-reference/guides/knowledge-base#import-online-documents-and-drive-files).

get.description:
Lists the query records of a knowledge base, newest first. Each [Run Query](/en/api-reference/queries/run-query) call saves a record once its stream opens, including a run that then fails, unless the client disconnected or the run failed with `RETRIEVAL_EXECUTION_LEASE_LOST`.

The list contains the records this key produced plus records produced by workflows, agents, MCP clients, and other API keys. A separate key for each tenant does not limit this list to that tenant's runs. Retrieval tests run in Dify are never listed.

`source` is the only filter. Capture the `x-query-run-id` header of [Run Query](/en/api-reference/queries/run-query) at query time to reach one run again.

For how to read a run's chunks, conflicts, and missing chunks together, see [Investigate an Answer](/en/api-reference/guides/knowledge-base#investigate-an-answer).

completed.description: `true` when the run answered, `false` when it failed. Every listed run has finished, so `false` never means still running.

duration_ms.description: Duration of the run in milliseconds. `null` when not recorded.

evidence_bundle_id.description: ID of the set of retrieved chunks the record refers to. No operation takes this ID. The three chunk views take the query record ID. `null` when the run recorded none.

evidence_state.description: How well the retrieved chunks support an answer: `answerable`, `partial`, `not-enough-evidence`, `conflict`, or `permission-limited`. `null` when the run recorded none.

final_score.description: Highest final relevance score across the run's retrieved chunks, from 0 to 1. `null` when nothing was scored.

id.description: Query record ID. Equals the `x-query-run-id` response header of the [Run Query](/en/api-reference/queries/run-query) call that produced it.

mode.description: Retrieval depth of the run: `fast`, `deep`, or `research`.

open_bad_case_id.description: ID of the unresolved bad case opened on this record under **Quality** in Dify. No operation in this API takes this ID. `null` when none is open.

profile.description: Models and index versions in effect during the run. Each field is `null` when not recorded.

embedding_vector_space_id.description: ID of the vector space the embeddings live in.

projection_publication_id.description: ID of the index publication the run searched. Compare it across records to see whether two runs searched the same index.

retrieval_profile_revision.description: Revision of the knowledge base's retrieval settings at run time.

query_images.description: Images used in the original query, when present. Omitted for text-only queries.

byte_size.description: File size in bytes, or `null` when unavailable.

name.description: File name. May be `null` in Service API responses.

preview_url.description: Preview URL. May be `null` in Service API responses; do not depend on it to display the image.

upload_file_id.description: ID of the image file used in the original query.

result_count.description: Number of retrieved chunks the run returned.

scores.description: Highest score of each kind across the run's retrieved chunks, each from 0 to 1 or `null` when not computed.

source.description: Who produced the record: `service_api` (API key callers, including this API), `workflow` (a workflow node), `agent`, `mcp`, or `retrieval_test` (a Dify retrieval test).

stages.description: Summaries of the run's recorded steps, in execution order: each step's name, status, and candidate count when available. Call [Get Query Record](/en/api-reference/query-records/get-query-record) with this record's ID for step metadata, including the depth decision and answer summary.

candidate_count.description: Number of candidates the step recorded. Only Dify retrieval tests record it, so it is `null` on every other record.

status.description: `ok`, `error`, or `skipped`.

next_cursor.description: Cursor for the next page, or `null` on the last page. Send it back as `cursor`.

get.description:
Returns one query record in full: the query, the retrieval depth, who ran it, and the pipeline steps in execution order with their metadata. The `query.generate` step's metadata embeds every retrieved chunk, so the response can be large (up to 2 MiB).

Chunks from documents deleted since the run show as unavailable. For paginated views of the same chunks, use [List Query Chunks](/en/api-reference/query-records/list-query-chunks), [List Query Conflicts](/en/api-reference/query-records/list-query-conflicts), and [List Missing Chunks](/en/api-reference/query-records/list-missing-chunks).

For the models and index versions the run used, read `profile` in [List Query Records](/en/api-reference/query-records/list-query-records).

For how to read a run's chunks, conflicts, and missing chunks together, see [Investigate an Answer](/en/api-reference/guides/knowledge-base#investigate-an-answer).

parameters.description: Knowledge base ID: the last segment of the Service API endpoint shown in the knowledge base's **API Access** dialog (`…/knowledge-fs/spaces/<knowledge base ID>`), and the segment after `/datasets/new/` in the address bar.
parameters.name: knowledge_base_id

parameters.description: Query record ID: the `x-query-run-id` response header of [Run Query](/en/api-reference/queries/run-query), or `id` from [List Query Records](/en/api-reference/query-records/list-query-records).
parameters.name: query_record_id

items.text: Refunds are issued within 14 days of purchase.

created_at.description: When the run was recorded, ISO 8601.

evidence_bundle_id.description: ID of the set of retrieved chunks the record refers to. No operation takes this ID. The chunks themselves are embedded in the `query.generate` step. `null` when the run recorded none.

knowledge_space_id.description: Internal ID of the knowledge base. Not the knowledge base ID in the path.

mode.description: Retrieval depth of the run: `fast`, `deep`, or `research`.

query_images.description: Images used in the original query, when present. Omitted for text-only queries.

byte_size.description: File size in bytes, or `null` when unavailable.

upload_file_id.description: ID of the image file used in the original query.

steps.description: Steps of the run, in execution order.

ended_at.description: When the step ended, ISO 8601. `null` when not recorded.

metadata.description: Step details. The available keys depend on the step. Handle additional metadata keys without assuming a fixed set.

degraded.description: `query.route`: whether the depth decision fell back because the reasoning model's depth call failed.

durationMs.description: `query.route`: time the depth decision took, in milliseconds.

eventCount.description: `query.generate`: number of events the run recorded, including internal ones. Not the number of stream events sent.

evidenceBundle.description:
Recorded on the `query.generate` step. Find it by scanning `steps[]` for this key rather than by step name. The retrieved chunks the three list views are derived from.

Citation `startOffset` and `endOffset` values are zero-based UTF-8 byte offsets in parsed document text, with an inclusive start and exclusive end. These are not positions in the original file or answer.

createdAt.description: When the chunks were recorded, ISO 8601.

id.description: ID of this set of retrieved chunks.

items.description: The retrieved chunks, in the order the run ranked them.

citations.description: Where the chunk comes from. The first is the primary citation.

documentAssetId.description: Document file ID. To find its document, pass it with `documentVersion` to [Get Document by File](/en/api-reference/documents-and-chunks/get-document-by-file).

withNodeId.description: Chunk ID it conflicts with. Present when known.

metadata.description: Free-form chunk metadata.

missingEvidence.description: Chunks the run expected but could not use.

expectedEvidenceId.description: Chunk ID that was expected. Present when known.

metadata.description: Free-form record metadata.

reason.description:
`not-retrieved`, `permission-filtered`, `stale`, `conflict`, or `unknown`.

`permission-filtered`: An access check excluded the chunk.

text.description: What was missing. Only available here. The missing-chunks view omits it.

failedQueryTrigger.description: `query.generate`: why the run counts as a failed query: `no-retrieval-evidence` or `low-confidence`. Present only when `queryOutcome` is `no-evidence` or `low-confidence`. These runs still complete normally.

finishReason.description: `query.generate`: why generation stopped: `retrieval-evidence` when chunks were found, `no-retrieval-evidence` when nothing matched.

itemCount.description: `query.retrieve`: number of chunks the retrieval returned.

queryOutcome.description: `query.generate`: classification of the run, for example `answered`.

requestedMode.description: `query.route`: the depth the caller asked for, or the knowledge base's default depth when the caller omitted `mode`. `selectionSource` tells the two apart.

resolver.description: `query.route`: how the depth was chosen, for example `explicit` when the request or the default named a depth.

selectionSource.description: `query.route`: where the requested depth came from: `request`, `profile-default`, or `legacy-default`.

name.description: Step name. `query.route` is the depth decision and `query.generate` the answer summary. Between them the retrieval pipeline writes `query.embed`, `query.retrieve`, and `query.answer`.

status.description: `ok`, `error`, or `skipped`.

Entries follow the order of the retrieved chunks, then conflict order within each chunk. An empty `data` with `truncated: false` means the run recorded no conflicts.

**Available for**: Workflow apps.

Run the app's published workflow and return its outputs, either in a single `blocking` response or as a `streaming` Server-Sent Events feed. Requires a published workflow.

inputs.query: Translate this to French: Hello world
Summarize this text: The quick brown fox jumps over the lazy dog.

schema.description:
A stream of Server-Sent Events. Parse it per the [SSE Streaming guide](/en/api-reference/guides/streaming): read `data:` lines, dispatch on the `event` field, skip `ping` (keep-alive; the stream opens with one, then more arrive roughly every 10 seconds).

**Stream lifecycle**: The stream closes when a `workflow_finished`, `workflow_paused`, or `error` event is received. Errors are delivered in-stream with HTTP status `200`; inspect the event payload for details rather than relying on the status code.

**Reasoning events**:
- `reasoning_chunk`: A chain-of-thought delta from an LLM node whose `reasoning_format` is `separated`. Concatenate consecutive `reasoning_chunk` events to rebuild the full reasoning; an event with `is_final: true` marks the node finished thinking (and may carry an empty `reasoning`). The payload sits under `data` and, unlike chat apps, carries `message_id: null` and no `conversation_id`. The parallel `text_chunk` stream stays free of `<think>` tags.

**Human Input events**:
- `human_input_required`: Fires together with `workflow_paused` when the workflow reaches a Human Input node. Use the `form_token` from the payload to drive the form-handling flow via the [Human Input API](/en/api-reference/human-input/get-human-input-form).
- `human_input_form_filled`: A recipient submitted the form; workflow execution resumes.
- `human_input_form_timeout`: The form expired without a response. Workflow follows the timeout fallback edge if defined.

200.description:
Successful response. The content type and structure depend on the `response_mode` parameter in the request.

- If `response_mode` is `blocking`, returns `application/json` with a `WorkflowBlockingResponse` object.
- If `response_mode` is `streaming`, returns `text/event-stream` with a stream of `ChunkWorkflowEvent` objects.

Returned in the `workflow_id` field of [Run Workflow](/en/api-reference/workflow-runs/run-workflow) responses and [Get Workflow Run Detail](/en/api-reference/workflow-runs/get-workflow-run-detail). Must reference a published version; a draft version ID is rejected with `bad_request`.
parameters.name: workflow_id

schema.description:
A stream of Server-Sent Events. Parse it per the [SSE Streaming guide](/en/api-reference/guides/streaming): read `data:` lines, dispatch on the `event` field, skip `ping` (keep-alive; the stream opens with one, then more arrive roughly every 10 seconds).

**Stream lifecycle**: The stream closes when a `workflow_finished`, `workflow_paused`, or `error` event is received. Errors are delivered in-stream with HTTP status `200`; inspect the event payload for details rather than relying on the status code.

**Reasoning events**:
- `reasoning_chunk`: A chain-of-thought delta from an LLM node whose `reasoning_format` is `separated`. Concatenate consecutive `reasoning_chunk` events to rebuild the full reasoning; an event with `is_final: true` marks the node finished thinking (and may carry an empty `reasoning`). The payload sits under `data` and, unlike chat apps, carries `message_id: null` and no `conversation_id`. The parallel `text_chunk` stream stays free of `<think>` tags.

**Human Input events**:
- `human_input_required`: Fires together with `workflow_paused` when the workflow reaches a Human Input node. Use the `form_token` from the payload to drive the form-handling flow via the [Human Input API](/en/api-reference/human-input/get-human-input-form).
- `human_input_form_filled`: A recipient submitted the form; workflow execution resumes.
- `human_input_form_timeout`: The form expired without a response. Workflow follows the timeout fallback edge if defined.

200.description:
Successful response. The content type and structure depend on the `response_mode` parameter in the request.

- If `response_mode` is `blocking`, returns `application/json` with a `WorkflowBlockingResponse` object.
- If `response_mode` is `streaming`, returns `text/event-stream` with a stream of `ChunkWorkflowEvent` objects.

get.description: Returns the available models of a given type. Use it to find the `text-embedding` and `rerank` models to configure on a knowledge base.

parameters.description: Type of model to retrieve. For knowledge base configuration, use `text-embedding` for embedding models or `rerank` for reranking models.
parameters.name: model_type

data.description: List of model providers with their available models.

icon_small.description: URL of the provider's small icon.

icon_small_dark.description: Dark-mode icon URLs; `null` when the provider has none.

label.description: Localized display name of the provider.

models.description: List of available models from this provider.

features.description: Supported features of the model, `null` if none.

fetch_from.description: Where the model definition comes from. `predefined-model` for built-in models, `customizable-model` for user-configured models.

has_invalid_load_balancing_configs.description: Whether the model has invalid load-balancing configurations.

label.description: Localized display name of the model.

load_balancing_enabled.description: Whether load balancing is enabled for the model.

model.description: Model identifier. Use this as the `embedding_model` value when creating or updating a knowledge base.

model_type.description: Type of the model, matching the `model_type` path parameter.

status.description: Model availability status. `active` when ready to use.

provider.description: Model provider identifier, formatted as `organization/plugin_name/provider_name` (e.g. `langgenius/openai/openai`). Legacy providers may return the bare short form (e.g. `openai`).

status.description: Provider status. `active` when credentials are configured and valid.

tenant_id.description: Workspace ID the provider configuration belongs to.

200.description: Available models for the specified type.

servers.description: Base URL of the Dify Service API. For self-hosted deployments, replace it with your own API base URL.

api_base_url.description: Host and path of the API base URL, without the `https://` prefix.
